statement_record.book: An abelian category is a category satisfying four axioms: (a) it has a zero object (simultaneously initial and terminal); (b) it has all binary products and all binary coproducts; (c) every morphism has a kernel and a cokernel, the kernel (cokernel) of f being the equalizer (coequalizer) of f with the zero map; (d) every monomorphism is a kernel of some map and every epimorphism is a cokernel of some map.
statement_record.intree: Class Abelian (C : Category) := { abelian_additive : @Additive C; abelian_kernels : @HasKernels C (@additive_zero C abelian_additive); abelian_cokernels : @HasCokernels C (@additive_zero C abelian_additive); abelian_monic_normal {x y} (f : x ~> y) : Monic f → IsKernel (`1 (`2 (cokernel f))) f; abelian_epic_normal {x y} (f : x ~> y) : Epic f → IsCokernel (`1 (`2 (kernel f))) f } — where Additive bundles ZeroObject + Preadditive (padd/pzero, bilinear composition) + HasBiproducts + pneg with padd_pneg, and IsKernel f i := IsEqualizer f zero_mor k i.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger (as a definition it demands strictly more data, so a priori fewer instances): clause (a) matches exactly (@ZeroObject C is Terminal + Initial with a coincidence iso), clause (c) matches exactly and literally as the equalizer/coequalizer against zero_mor, clause (d) matches exactly (both normality directions, pinned at the CHOSEN cokernel/kernel, which Structure/Kernel.v's kernel_of_any_cokernel shows costs no generality). Clause (b) is strengthened from 'binary products and binary coproducts' to HasBiproducts (a single object that is simultaneously product and coproduct with the delta relations), and the class additionally carries the whole Ab-enrichment (Preadditive's padd/pzero with bilinear composition, plus Additive's pneg and padd_pneg) as ASSUMED FIELDS — exactly the structure Riehl derives from (a)-(d) in her unnumbered remark. Classically the two axiomatizations pick out the same categories; in-tree that equivalence is not proved.

statement_record.book: In an abelian category finite products and finite coproducts coincide: the canonical comparison map from the coproduct to the product (identities on matching summands, zero maps off the diagonal) is an isomorphism, and the common object is called the biproduct or direct sum.
statement_record.intree: The notion is the record `Biproduct x y` (one object carrying injections and projections with bi_exl ∘ bi_inl ≈ id, bi_exr ∘ bi_inr ≈ id, the mixed composites ≈ zero_mor, and BOTH universal properties bi_is_product and bi_is_coproduct). The comparison map itself is `can_comparison (x y : C) : x + y ~> x × y := (id △ zero_mor) ▽ (zero_mor △ id)` with its four matrix-entry lemmas, and the coincidence claim is proved only in the form `cartesian_biproduct (x y : C) : Biproduct x y` with biproduct_obj := x × y, under a Preadditive (CMon-enrichment) hypothesis rather than under Riehl's abelian axioms.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the biproduct object and the comparison morphism are both in-tree, and the coincidence IS proved — but from a hypothesis Riehl does not have (an assumed Preadditive enrichment) instead of from the abelian axioms, and in the 'every product is also a coproduct' form rather than as invertibility of can_comparison. Nothing in-tree asserts `IsIsomorphism (can_comparison x y)`; in Structure/Semiadditive.v that is a section HYPOTHESIS (`Context (E : ∀ x y : C, IsIsomorphism (can_comparison x y))`, line 324), and Structure/Abelian.v sidesteps the question entirely by assuming `additive_biproducts : HasBiproducts` in the class.

statement_record.book: The axioms of Definition E.5.1 imply that every hom-set of an abelian category canonically carries an abelian-group structure whose identity is the zero map and for which composition is bilinear; equivalently, an abelian category is canonically enriched over (Ab, ⊗_Z, Z). statement_record.book: The image of a morphism in an abelian category is defined to be the kernel of its cokernel, or equivalently the cokernel of its kernel; in an abelian category these two objects are always isomorphic, so the definition is unambiguous.

evidence.intree_statement: Lemma monic_iff_kernel_pzero {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : Monic f ↔ (∀ (z : C) (u : z ~> x), f ∘ u ≈ zero_mor → u ≈ zero_mor).
Lemma epic_iff_cokernel_pzero {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : Epic f ↔ (∀ (z : C) (u : y ~> z), u ∘ f ≈ zero_mor → u ≈ zero_mor).
Lemma strong_epi_mono_is_iso {C : Category} {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : StrongEpi f → Monic f → IsIsomorphism f.  Lemma abelian_epic_strong {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : Epic f → StrongEpi f.

statement_record.book: Exercise E.5.i, in an arbitrary abelian category: (i) if f satisfies 'f ∘ g = 0 implies g = 0' then f is a monomorphism, and dually for epimorphisms; (ii) a morphism that is both a monomorphism and an epimorphism is an isomorphism (the category is balanced); (iii) the short five lemma — in a commutative ladder of two short exact sequences with vertical maps a, b, c, if a and c are both monic, both epic, or both isomorphisms then so is b.
statement_record.intree: Part (i) is `monic_iff_kernel_pzero : Monic f ↔ (∀ z (u : z ~> x), f ∘ u ≈ zero_mor → u ≈ zero_mor)` and its dual `epic_iff_cokernel_pzero : Epic f ↔ (∀ z (u : y ~> z), u ∘ f ≈ zero_mor → u ≈ zero_mor)`, both in the `Context {A : @Abelian C}` section. Part (ii) is not stated, but follows in one step from `abelian_epic_strong : Epic f → StrongEpi f` and `strong_epi_mono_is_iso : StrongEpi f → Monic f → IsIsomorphism f`. Part (iii) has no in-tree counterpart.
statement_record.strength_comparison: mixed. Part (i): intree-stronger — Riehl asks only for the implication (zero-cancellation ⇒ monic), the in-tree lemmas are biconditionals, in exactly the abelian setting, and are the workhorses of the file. Part (ii): the content is available but only as a two-lemma composite, never asserted as 'Abelian C → mono ∧ epi → iso'; note the route runs through normality (epi ⇒ conormal ⇒ regular epi ⇒ strong epi), which is faithful to the intended proof. Part (iii): absent.

gap: Part (iii), the short five lemma, is entirely missing and is not currently statable: the library has no exact-sequence predicate (see riehl:E.5:def-exact-sequence — grep for 'exact sequence'/'short exact'/'IsExact' finds only prose), so neither the two short exact rows nor the commuting ladder can be expressed. Part (ii) is not stated as a lemma: the balancedness of an abelian category must be assembled by the reader from `abelian_epic_strong` (Structure/Abelian.v:422) and `strong_epi_mono_is_iso` (Structure/Factorization/StrongEpi.v:154); grep for 'balanced' finds only the unrelated balanced-monoidal development (Structure/Monoidal/Balanced.v). Part (i) is fully present and stronger than asked.
